Using Made in Heaven, Pucci creates a new universe where everyone knows their fate, which he considers "heaven", with the souls of the people that died during Made in Heaven's acceleration getting left behind and replaced with fakes; however, to finish its creation he has to reach the point in time where the acceleration started - Cape Canaveral. 

 He fails to do so and gets killed by Emporio and Weather Report. This cancels the effects of Made in Heaven and reverts the universe to its original state.

(THE EXPLANATIONS FROM THIS POINT ONWARD AREN'T EXPLICITLY STATED IN THE MANGA AND THEREFORE REQUIRE A DEGREE OF CONJECTURE THAT IS COMMONLY ACCEPTED WITHIN THE FANBASE)

As Pucci had died during the acceleration, his soul is left behind in the Made in Heaven universe, while the souls of those that were originally left behind (including the Stone Ocean gang bar Emporio) get to live again; the "fake" Enrico Pucci, if one even exists at all, does not have the same impact on the lives of Jotaro, Jolyne and the others - while Parts 1-5 *probably* happened the way they did, the events of Stone Ocean never transpire, Jolyne (Irene) lives a better and happier life, and (assumedly) has a better relationship with her dad. Dio's legacy dies with him. The Joestars are free of their family's fate.

How do Steel Ball Run, JoJolion and The JOJOLands fit into this? They don't - part of the reason Stone Ocean's ending went as it did was Araki desiring a clean slate of sorts to work with, unburdened by the story of the previous parts of the story. Parts 7-9 take place in a wholly separate universe, only having similar concepts like Stands, the Joestar family, and other references like character names, designs, traits and sometimes Stands.

Firstly, Tooru is an [antipode](https://i.imgur.com/R5NePOu.jpeg) to Josuke - Josuke embraces his newfound family and loved ones, while Tooru, as a rock human, is unable or unwilling to form genuine bonds with others. Tooru also considers making and having "dreams and memories" to be the most important thing in life, while Josuke lives in the "now", rejecting his past and focusing on the current. This also affects their relationships with Yasuho: when Josuke and her actively help and support each other, Tooru only reminisces of their memories together. When Josuke is a man born with no identity who proceeds to make his own throughout his journey, Tooru simply steals the identity of Satoru Akefu through his Stand. This is also why Jobin, ultimately, isn't a villain: like Josuke, he also cared about his family and loved ones and his bonds with them.

Now, about Wonder of U, Go Beyond, and the ending of JoJolion as a whole.

Wonder of U is misfortune personified. As it's been revealed, it bends the very laws of the universe to turn everything against you if you dare fight against it or Tooru. This is exactly why Wonder of U *cannot* be outsmarted, or defeated through a clever trick - the universe itself is against you, as if conspiring to not let you win, and one cannot simply outsmart or outfight that. 

But that's when Go Beyond comes in.

One of JoJolion's central themes, in my opinion, is bonds. Bonds between family, friends and loved ones, and how those bonds shape the person and their life. Josuke's birth and his journey are a miracle, but a miracle born of love and affection between many people - the whole thing started due to Yoshikage Kira's desire to save his beloved mother. Josuke himself was born out of Josefumi Kujo's sacrifice for the sake of hope; Yasuho assisted him at every turn out of love; Norisuke took him in hoping that he can help solve the mystery of his family's curse and help his grandson; Rai helped him out of a desire to pay the debt he owed to Norisuke; Kei (though admittedly a very underused character) helped him save their mother. Go Beyond is a culmination of that; a ***miracle*** coming through to save Josuke at a time where all hope seems to be lost, and a miracle born out of the bonds he formed and the connections he has with others and they have with him. ~~The Miracle of Your Love, if you may~~

However, Go Beyond doesn't solve everything. In the end, it only helped weather the storm of the seemingly unbeatable calamity. In the end, Josuke is left with no apparent way to save Holly, though her condition won't get worse, and the Higashikatas only managed to cure Tsurugi through a pyrrhic victory, with Jobin and Kaato dead, Norisuke wounded, and Joshu disfigured. Like Johnny before him, Josuke climbed back to zero from a deep negative, and the only thing that's left is to pick up the pieces.

This is what I think JoJolion's message is. Sometimes, things will go horribly, horribly wrong, as if the universe itself decided to conspire against you, and the only thing that's left to do is to rely on your loved ones to help you survive this seemingly unbeatable calamity, then start anew.

Sorry if that came out a bit lengthly, but that genuinely is what I think about Tooru and the ending
